title: GOV-0121: DISCOVERED — the doctrine file is section-scoped by `## ` headings; 32 token assertions depend on heading depth and nothing tells an editor
problem:
🧠 **ARCHI (BARCHI-2)** — DISCOVERED while editing `GITHUB_CONTROL_PLANE.md` in PR #278. **Nobody's fault in that PR; filed separately per *Discovery ≠ scope expansion*.**

**Id claim:** `GOV-0121`. Ceiling swept at time of filing: **`GOV-0120`** (main tree, issue titles+bodies, issue comments, all remote branch heads). Next free ≥ `GOV-0122`.

## The hazard

`docs/governance/GITHUB_CONTROL_PLANE.md` is edited constantly by governance seats writing prose. Two tests scope assertions to a *section*, delimited by the **next `## ` heading**:

```python
# tests/test_badf_build_activation.py
start = text.find("## badf-build → ACTIVE"); self.assertGreater(start, 0, "no BLD-E admission section")
end = text.find("\n## ", start + 1); section = text[start:end if end > 0 else None]
for token in (...16 tokens...): self.assertIn(token, section, token)

# tests/test_badf_git_activation.py — same shape, 15 tokens
```

**An inserted `## ` heading anywhere inside an admission section truncates it, and the token assertions fail.** **32** token assertions across the two modules sit behind heading depth.

> **Counts corrected after filing (BADF-REV, verified independently here by AST).** The original body said 31, from a grep that quietly merged two loops with *different* scoping. Measured by walking the `For` nodes and reading each `assertIn`'s second argument:
>
> ```
> build_activation:46    8 tokens -> assertIn(..., src)       NOT heading-coupled
> build_activation:54   17 tokens -> assertIn(..., section)   coupled
> git_activation:59     15 tokens -> assertIn(..., section)   coupled
> ```
>
> So: **32 coupled** (17+15), not 31 — and separately, **8 of build's tokens assert against the whole source and cannot be broken by a heading at all.** The number is the part of a reader prices, and "16 tokens in the section" merged a coupled loop with an uncoupled one. Grep counts statements; the property is tuple length against a *specific target*, and only the AST distinguishes them.

A third module asserts on the whole file, including a **negative**:

```python
# tests/test_badf_traceability.py:171-172
self.assertIn("wp/WP-2026-NNNN-<slug>", plane)
self.assertNotIn("wp/BADF-WP-NNNN", plane)     # breakable ONLY by adding text
```

## Measured, not reasoned — the tripwire fired

Mutation with a negative control, on `83f0472`:

```
NEGATIVE CONTROL (unmutated)                     GREEN  OK
MUTANT ('## ' inserted inside the badf-build section)  RED  FAILED (failures=1)
RESTORED                                         GREEN  OK
```

## Severity, corrected downward from how I first framed it

The phrasing that came up in review was *"silently truncates."* **That is wrong and the correction matters.** The failure is **loud** — RED at test time, with the offending token named. What is invisible is the *edit-time* model: someone writing prose has no reason to treat heading depth as load-bearing, and nothing in the document says it is.

So this is **not** a vacuity bug — it is the good kind of guard, failing closed. It is a **latent-hazard/ergonomics** issue: the control is sound, the affordance is missing. Filing it at that severity rather than the more dramatic one.

## Why it is worth filing anyway

In #278 I added 18 lines to this file and used `### ` rather than `## `. That was **correct by luck** — I chose the depth because it read better under the existing `##`, not because I knew 31 assertions depended on it. A 1-in-2 coin flip on an aesthetic judgement, in a file governance seats edit constantly. The next editor gets the same coin flip.

Credit: BADF-REV raised it during the #278 review after I said the safety was mechanism-not-judgment; the mutation proof and the severity correction are mine.

## Proposed shape (not a plan — no id claimed for a WP)

Cheapest first, per the minimality ladder:

1. **A comment in the doctrine file itself**, at the top of each admission section: *"section-scoped by the next `## `; inserting a `## ` heading inside this section breaks N token assertions in `tests/test_badf_<x>_activation.py`."* One line each, where the editor is actually looking.
2. Optionally, a comment in the two tests naming the coupling from the other side.

**Explicitly NOT proposed:** rewriting the section-scoping to be more robust. It works, it fails closed, and replacing a working control to improve an affordance is the over-engineering the Lean gate exists to prevent. The gap is that the document does not tell its editors what the tests assume.

## Scope of the pattern — swept and closed (BADF-REV; re-verified here)

I filed this saying I had *not* checked whether other docs share the coupling. That is now closed, and the answer is **no**:

```
modules slicing a doc by "## " :  3
  test_badf_build_activation.py     live scoping
  test_badf_git_activation.py       live scoping
  test_no_dead_assertions.py        FALSE POSITIVE
```

The third is a `STRING_HASH = ''' ... '''` synthetic fixture — the dead-assertion detector's **own negative control** for a `#` inside a string literal, not live scoping code. Read before reporting, by both seats. `docs/00-operating-model.md`, the only other doc read by name, is used purely as a scratch file in the git tests (`write_text("stash me")`).

**So the pattern is exactly these two modules.** The issue does not understate it.

*(There is a small recursion worth noting: that fixture exists because of an earlier instance of this same class — a naive `grep -nE '#.*self\.assert'` false-positiving on this very file, where the `#` lives inside the string `"## badf-build -> ACTIVE"`. The detector was given a negative control precisely so it would not ship a false positive as its remedy.)*

**Version tier:** patch (comments/docs only). **Review:** whoever takes it; not `contract_changed`, not `behavior_changed`.
